outcome: No result found addressing whether outer billiards relative to almost every convex polygon have unbounded orbits; the question remains open, and all activity found in the window concerns either unrelated variants of outer billiards or a distinct sub-question (aperiodic orbits on regular polygons) that does not settle unboundedness.
summary: This bullet is a compound/umbrella entry ('many problems concerning an outer billiard'), with the almost-every-convex-polygon unbounded-orbit question as its headline example. This is the classical Moser-Neumann question, dating to the 1950s-1970s, on which Schwartz (2007-2009, kites) and Dolgopyat-Fayad (2008, semidisks/circular caps) established the only known affirmative instances prior to the frozen revision -- both predate the window and are recorded here only as background. I confirmed via the current Wikipedia outer-billiards article that the 'almost every convex polygon' unbounded-orbit question is still listed as open as of today (2026-09-22), with kites and near-semidisks remaining the only known shapes (up to affine transformation) giving unbounded orbits. I searched arXiv broadly for 2024-2026 work on outer billiards and unbounded orbits and found only: (1) variant systems with different definitions -- 'outer length billiards' (arXiv:2510.11869, Oct 2025) and 'bouncing outer billiards' (arXiv:2410.17985, Oct 2024), which change the map/rule rather than restricting the classical outer-billiard map to a subclass of polygons, so under the scope rule (S3.1) these are related problems, not cases; (2) 'Aperiodic points for outer billiards' (arXiv:2311.09643, latest v4 Feb 2025), which proves Schwartz's ICM-2022 conjecture that outer billiards on regular N-gons (N>4, N!=6) have aperiodic orbits -- a genuine advance, but aperiodicity is a distinct property from unboundedness (an orbit can be aperiodic yet bounded), and it concerns only regular polygons, a measure-zero subset of convex polygons, so it does not bear on the 'almost every convex polygon' claim; (3) a paper on Ivrii's conjecture for outer/symplectic billiards (arXiv:2402.18782) concerning periodic orbits, unrelated to unboundedness; (4) 'Elliptic islands and zero measure escaping orbits in a class of outer billiards' (arXiv:2506.18433 / DCDS 2025), which studies circular sectors (not polygons) and is about a different geometric family. None of these results restrict or settle the stated question for convex polygons. I found no survey (including a 2026 open-problems-in-billiards survey, arXiv:2602.12896) that reports any progress on this specific conjecture since 2024. No AI system appears anywhere in this literature. I agree with the triage's 'none' verdict.
competing_reading: One could argue the aperiodic-points result (arXiv:2311.09643) is worth recording as 'partial' progress on the broader 'many problems concerning an outer billiard' umbrella bullet, since it resolves a named conjecture (Schwartz's ICM-2022 aperiodicity conjecture) that is explicitly one of the 'many problems' about outer billiards in this area, even though it is not the specific unbounded-orbits-for-almost-every-polygon example given in the statement. Under a looser reading of the umbrella statement, this could be classified as `partial` with `resolution_direction` confirmed. I did not adopt this reading because the statement singles out the almost-every-polygon unbounded-orbit question as its concrete example ('for example, showing...'), and the aperiodicity question is a materially different property (aperiodic vs. unbounded) on a different, measure-zero subclass (regular polygons vs. almost every convex polygon), so it does not change what a careful reader would write in this specific bullet.
what_would_settle_it: A paper proving (or disproving) unboundedness of outer-billiard orbits for a positive-measure or generic/residual set of convex polygons, or extending the known unbounded-orbit examples beyond kites and near-semidisks to a broader class recognized as progress toward 'almost every' polygon.
